title: Falsafa va axloq mavzularida munozara
goal_uz: Dars oxirida mavhum axloqiy atamalarni to‘g‘ri artikl bilan ishlatasiz, asos va xulosadan iborat mantiqiy dalil qurasiz, mantiqiy xatolarni nomlaysiz, fikriy tajribalarni shart gaplar bilan bayon qilasiz va yon berib, hurmat bilan e’tiroz bildirgan holda uch daqiqalik munozara olib borasiz.

vocab.uz: o‘z irodasi bilan qaror qilish huquqi

scenes.title: Falsafiy munozara
board: Debating Philosophy and Ethics
(Falsafa va axloq mavzularida munozara)
vocabulary · logic · thought experiments · respectful disagreement
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda adabiy matnni tahlil qildik: vosita, g‘oya va uslubni tezis atrofida tushuntirdik. Bugun tahlildan bahsga o‘tamiz. Dars oxirida axloqiy tushunchalarni aniq nomlaysiz, mantiqiy dalil qurasiz, fikriy tajribalarni tilga olasiz va raqibingizga hurmat bilan e’tiroz bildirib, uch daqiqalik munozara olib borasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we analysed literary texts. Today we move from analysis to argument: debating questions of right and wrong with precision, logic and courtesy.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. Oldingi safar adabiy matnlarni tahlil qildik. Bugun tahlildan bahsga o‘tamiz: to‘g‘ri va noto‘g‘ri haqidagi savollarni aniqlik, mantiq va xushmuomalalik bilan muhokama qilamiz.

scenes.title: Asosiy axloqiy tushunchalar
board: morality (axloq) · ethics (axloq falsafasi)
virtue (fazilat) · duty (burch) · conscience (vijdon)
autonomy (mustaqil irodalilik) · dignity (qadr-qimmat)

examples.t: Respect for autonomy lies at the heart of medical ethics.
examples.uz: Shaxs irodasini hurmat qilish tibbiyot etikasining markazida turadi.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi nuqta: mavhum axloqiy lug‘at. Morality kishining yoki jamiyatning amaldagi axloqiy qarashlari, ethics esa ular haqidagi tizimli fikr, ya’ni axloq falsafasi. Virtue fazilat, duty burch, conscience vijdon. Autonomy shaxsning o‘zi haqida o‘zi qaror qilish huquqi, dignity esa insonning qadr-qimmati. Bu so‘zlar bahsning “g‘ishtlari”.
scenes.say: Morality refers to the values people actually hold; ethics is the systematic study of them. Debates turn on concepts such as virtue, duty, conscience, autonomy and dignity, so use them precisely.
scenes.say_uz: Morality odamlar amalda ega bo‘lgan qadriyatlar, ethics esa ularni tizimli o‘rganish. Bahslar fazilat, burch, vijdon, mustaqil iroda va qadr-qimmat kabi tushunchalar atrofida aylanadi, shuning uchun ularni aniq ishlating.

scenes.title: Uch asosiy yondashuv
board: consequentialism: judge acts by outcomes
deontology: some acts are right or wrong in themselves
virtue ethics: what would a good person do?
scenes.say_native: Axloq falsafasida uchta katta yondashuv bor. Consequentialism, xususan utilitarianism, harakatni natijasiga qarab baholaydi. Deontology, ya’ni Kant an’anasi, ba’zi harakatlar, masalan yolg‘on, natijadan qat’i nazar noto‘g‘ri deydi. Virtue ethics, ya’ni Aristotel an’anasi, “yaxshi inson nima qilardi?” deb so‘raydi.
scenes.say: Consequentialists judge actions by their outcomes. Deontologists hold that certain acts, such as lying, are wrong in themselves, whatever the consequences. Virtue ethicists ask what a person of good character would do.
scenes.say_uz: Konsekvensialistlar harakatni natijasiga qarab baholaydi. Deontologlar yolg‘on kabi ba’zi harakatlar oqibatidan qat’i nazar o‘z-o‘zidan noto‘g‘ri deydi. Fazilat etikasi tarafdorlari esa yaxshi fe’lli inson nima qilishini so‘raydi.

scenes.title: Murakkabroq atamalar
board: intrinsic vs instrumental value
moral agent · culpability (aybdorlik)
relativism vs universalism
the greater good · a slippery notion

examples.t: Is knowledge intrinsically valuable, or merely instrumental?
examples.uz: Bilim o‘z-o‘zidan qimmatlimi yoki faqat vosita sifatidami?

scenes.say_native: C2 darajasida yana bir necha atama kerak. Intrinsic value narsaning o‘z-o‘zidan qimmati, instrumental value esa boshqa maqsadga vosita sifatidagi qimmati. Moral agent o‘z harakati uchun javobgar shaxs, culpability aybdorlik darajasi. Relativism axloq madaniyatga bog‘liq deydi, universalism esa umumbashariy axloqiy me’yorlar bor deb hisoblaydi.
scenes.say: Something has intrinsic value if it matters for its own sake, instrumental value if it serves another end. Relativists argue that morality varies by culture; universalists maintain that some norms bind everyone.
scenes.say_uz: Narsa o‘zi uchun muhim bo‘lsa, ichki qimmatga, boshqa maqsadga xizmat qilsa, vositaviy qimmatga ega. Relativistlar axloq madaniyatga qarab o‘zgaradi deydi, universalistlar esa ba’zi me’yorlar hammaga majburiy deb hisoblaydi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek va rus tili bilan qiyos
board: conscience (vijdon) ≠ consciousness (ong)
moral (adj.) ≠ morale (ruhiy holat)
ethics (fan) · an ethic (bitta tamoyil): a work ethic
рус. мораль ≈ morality, not 'a moral'
scenes.say_native: O‘zbekcha “axloq” ham morality, ham ethics ma’nosini beradi, inglizchada esa ular farqlanadi. Chalkash juftliklar: conscience vijdon, consciousness ong. Moral sifat yoki hikoya saboqi, morale esa jamoa ruhi. Ruscha “мораль” ko‘pincha morality ga mos, shuning uchun “the moral of society” emas, “social morality” deyiladi.
scenes.say: Watch the false friends. Conscience is your inner moral sense; consciousness is awareness. Morale means team spirit. And a work ethic is a single principle, whereas ethics is the whole field.
scenes.say_uz: Soxta do‘stlardan ehtiyot bo‘ling. Conscience ichki axloqiy tuyg‘u, consciousness esa ong. Morale jamoa ruhi. A work ethic bitta tamoyil, ethics esa butun soha.

scenes.title: Mavhum otlar va artikl
board: ✗ The justice is the most important value.
✓ Justice is the most important value.
✓ the justice of this decision (specific)
✗ The humanity must protect nature. → ✓ Humanity must...
scenes.say_native: Juda tipik xato: mavhum otlar oldidan “the” qo‘yish. Umumiy ma’noda justice, freedom, happiness, humanity artiklsiz ishlatiladi: “Justice is the most important value”. Faqat aniq holatga ishora qilsangiz “the” kerak: “the justice of this decision”. O‘zbek va rus tillarida artikl yo‘q, shuning uchun o‘quvchilar ba’zan hamma joyga “the” qo‘yib yuboradi.
scenes.say: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article: freedom matters, justice must be done. Add the only when the noun is made specific: the freedom of the press, the justice of this verdict.
scenes.say_uz: Umumiy ma’nodagi mavhum otlar artikl olmaydi: freedom matters, justice must be done. The faqat ot aniqlashganda qo‘shiladi: the freedom of the press, the justice of this verdict.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri atamani tanlang
board: 1 Judging an act only by its outcomes = ___
2 He acted against his ___. (conscience / consciousness)
3 ___ is essential in a democracy. (Freedom / The freedom)
4 Health has ___ value: it lets us pursue other goals.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta topshiriq. Birinchisida yondashuv nomini ayting. Ikkinchi va uchinchisida to‘g‘ri variantni tanlang, artiklga e’tibor bering. To‘rtinchisida intrinsic yoki instrumental so‘zlaridan birini qo‘ying va nega aynan u ekanini tushuntiring. Pauza oling va javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: One: judging an act only by its outcomes is called what? Two: he acted against his conscience, or consciousness. Three: freedom, or the freedom, is essential in a democracy. Four: health has what kind of value if it lets us pursue other goals?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: harakatni faqat natijasiga qarab baholash nima deyiladi? Ikki: u vijdoniga yoki ongiga qarshi ish qildi. Uch: freedom yoki the freedom demokratiyada zarur. To‘rt: sog‘liq boshqa maqsadlarga intilishga imkon bersa, qanday qimmatga ega?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 consequentialism
2 conscience
3 Freedom (no article)
4 instrumental (it may also be intrinsic)
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: consequentialism. Ikkinchi: conscience, chunki gap vijdon haqida. Uchinchi: “Freedom”, artiklsiz, chunki umumiy ma’no. To‘rtinchi: instrumental, chunki bu yerda sog‘liq boshqa maqsadlarga vosita sifatida ko‘rsatilgan. Biroq bahsda kimdir sog‘liq o‘z-o‘zidan ham qimmatli deyishi mumkin, aynan shunday nozik farqlar munozarani boyitadi.
scenes.say: Consequentialism; conscience; freedom, with no article; and instrumental, since health is valued here as a means. Someone could, of course, argue that health is intrinsically valuable too.
scenes.say_uz: Konsekvensializm; conscience; artiklsiz freedom; va instrumental, chunki sog‘liq bu yerda vosita sifatida qadrlanadi. Albatta, kimdir sog‘liq o‘z-o‘zidan ham qimmatli deb da’vo qilishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Asos va xulosa
board: premise → premise → conclusion
deductive: certain if premises are true
inductive: probable, based on evidence
It follows that... · Hence... · Granted that...

examples.t: All persons have dignity; prisoners are persons; it follows that prisoners have dignity.
examples.uz: Barcha shaxslar qadr-qimmatga ega; mahbuslar ham shaxs; demak, mahbuslar qadr-qimmatga ega.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi nuqta: mantiqiy dalil qurish. Har qanday dalilda premise, ya’ni asos, va conclusion, ya’ni xulosa bor. Deductive dalilda asoslar to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, xulosa albatta to‘g‘ri. Inductive dalil esa kuzatuvlarga tayanadi va xulosa faqat ehtimolli. Bog‘lovchilar: “It follows that”, “hence”, “granted that”, ya’ni “tan olaylik, ammo”.
scenes.say: Every argument moves from premises to a conclusion. A deductive argument guarantees its conclusion if the premises are true; an inductive one makes it probable. Signal the move clearly: it follows that, hence, therefore.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir dalil asoslardan xulosaga o‘tadi. Deduktiv dalil asoslar to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa xulosani kafolatlaydi, induktiv dalil esa uni ehtimolli qiladi. O‘tishni aniq bildiring: it follows that, hence, therefore.

scenes.title: Bahsli nutq tuzilmasi
board: 1 Claim  2 Reasons  3 Evidence / example
4 Anticipate the objection (steelman)
5 Rebut  6 Restate
scenes.say_native: Kuchli bahsli nutq olti qadamdan iborat: da’vo, sabablar, dalil yoki misol, raqibning eng kuchli e’tirozi, uni rad etish va da’voni qayta ta’kidlash. To‘rtinchi qadam steelmanning deyiladi: raqib fikrini eng kuchli shaklida bayon qilish. Bu straw man ning, ya’ni fikrni buzib ko‘rsatishning aksi, va tinglovchi ishonchini oshiradi.
scenes.say: A persuasive case states a claim, gives reasons and evidence, then confronts the strongest objection, the so-called steelman, before rebutting it. Engaging with the best version of your opponent's view makes your own far more credible.
scenes.say_uz: Ishonarli nutq da’voni aytadi, sabab va dalil keltiradi, so‘ng eng kuchli e’tirozga, ya’ni steelman ga duch keladi va uni rad etadi. Raqib fikrining eng yaxshi shakli bilan ishlash o‘z fikringizni ancha ishonchli qiladi.

scenes.title: Mantiqiy bog‘lovchilar
board: Given that... · Insofar as...
By the same token... · By extension...
Conversely... · Even if we grant that...
It does not follow that...

examples.t: Even if we grant that lying is sometimes kind, it does not follow that it is right.
examples.uz: Yolg‘on ba’zan mehribonlik ekanini tan olsak ham, bundan u to‘g‘ri degan xulosa chiqmaydi.

scenes.say_native: Bahsda mantiqiy bog‘lovchilar fikringiz yo‘nalishini ko‘rsatadi. “Given that” asosni beradi. “Insofar as” chegara qo‘yadi: “qaysidir darajada”. “By the same token” xuddi shu mantiqni boshqa holatga qo‘llaydi. “Conversely” teskari holatni beradi. Eng kuchli iboralardan biri: “It does not follow that”, ya’ni raqibning xulosasi asosidan kelib chiqmasligini ko‘rsatish.
scenes.say: Logical connectors map your reasoning for the listener. Even if we grant that is a powerful concession, and it does not follow that exposes a gap between someone's premise and their conclusion.
scenes.say_uz: Mantiqiy bog‘lovchilar fikringiz yo‘lini tinglovchiga ko‘rsatadi. Even if we grant that kuchli yon berish, it does not follow that esa kimningdir asosi va xulosasi orasidagi bo‘shliqni ochadi.

scenes.title: Mantiqiy xatolar
board: straw man · ad hominem
slippery slope · false dilemma
appeal to nature · hasty generalisation
scenes.say_native: Raqibning mantiqiy xatosini nomlay olish C2 belgisi. Straw man: raqib fikrini buzib, zaif shaklda rad etish. Ad hominem: fikrga emas, shaxsga hujum. Slippery slope: bir qadam muqarrar falokatga olib keladi degan asossiz da’vo. False dilemma: faqat ikki variant bor deb ko‘rsatish. Appeal to nature: tabiiy narsa albatta yaxshi deyish.
scenes.say: Learn to name common fallacies: the straw man, the ad hominem attack, the slippery slope, the false dilemma, the appeal to nature and the hasty generalisation. Naming a fallacy calmly is far more effective than raising your voice.
scenes.say_uz: Keng tarqalgan mantiqiy xatolarni nomlashni o‘rganing: soxta raqib, shaxsga hujum, sirpanchiq yo‘l, soxta dilemma, tabiatga murojaat va shoshma umumlashtirish. Xatoni xotirjam nomlash ovozni ko‘tarishdan ancha samarali.

scenes.title: Umumlashtirish va asossiz da’vo
board: ✗ Everybody knows that lying is always wrong.
✓ Many would argue that lying is wrong in most cases.
✗ Science proves that... (for a moral claim)
✓ The evidence suggests... but the moral question remains.
scenes.say_native: Tipik xato: “Everybody knows”, “always”, “never” kabi mutlaq so‘zlar. Ular raqibga bitta qarshi misol bilan sizni yiqitish imkonini beradi. Ikkinchi xato: axloqiy savolni faqat fakt bilan hal qilish. Fan nima borligini aytadi, nima qilish kerakligini esa o‘zi hal qilmaydi. Bu Devid Yum bilan bog‘liq “is–ought” muammosi.
scenes.say: Absolute claims invite a single counter-example. And beware of deriving an ought from an is: evidence tells us what is the case, but not, on its own, what ought to be done. Philosophers associate this gap with David Hume.
scenes.say_uz: Mutlaq da’volar bitta qarshi misolni chaqiradi. Bor narsadan kerak narsani chiqarishdan ehtiyot bo‘ling: dalil nima borligini aytadi, lekin o‘zicha nima qilish kerakligini aytmaydi. Faylasuflar bu bo‘shliqni Devid Yum nomi bilan bog‘laydi.

scenes.title: Xatoni nomlang
board: 1 You can't trust her view on poverty; she's rich.
2 If we allow this, soon society will collapse.
3 Either we ban cars or the planet dies.
4 So you're saying we should let criminals go free?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap, har birida bitta mantiqiy xato bor. Xatoni nomlang va nega xato ekanini inglizcha bir gap bilan tushuntiring, masalan, “This is an ad hominem because it attacks the person, not the argument”. Pauza oling, o‘ylab ko‘ring va javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: One: You can't trust her view on poverty; she's rich. Two: If we allow this, soon society will collapse. Three: Either we ban cars or the planet dies. Four: So you're saying we should let criminals go free?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Uning qashshoqlik haqidagi fikriga ishonib bo‘lmaydi, u boy. Ikki: Agar bunga ruxsat bersak, tez orada jamiyat qulaydi. Uch: Yo mashinalarni taqiqlaymiz, yo sayyora halok bo‘ladi. To‘rt: Demak, siz jinoyatchilarni qo‘yib yuborish kerak demoqchimisiz?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 ad hominem
2 slippery slope
3 false dilemma
4 straw man
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: ad hominem, chunki fikr emas, uning boyligi tanqid qilinyapti. Ikkinchi: slippery slope, falokatgacha zanjir isbotlanmagan. Uchinchi: false dilemma, oraliq yechimlar ko‘p. To‘rtinchi: straw man, raqib bunday demagan. Bunga “That’s not what I said” deb xotirjam javob berish mumkin.
scenes.say: One is an ad hominem; two, a slippery slope; three, a false dilemma, since many middle positions exist; and four, a straw man, which you might answer with: that is not what I said.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchisi shaxsga hujum, ikkinchisi sirpanchiq yo‘l, uchinchisi soxta dilemma, chunki ko‘p oraliq yechim bor, to‘rtinchisi soxta raqib, unga “men bunday demadim” deb javob berish mumkin.

scenes.title: Namunaviy bahsli nutq
board: Motion: Lying is never morally justified.
Listen for: claim · reasons · steelman · rebuttal
scenes.say_native: Endi munozarachining qisqa nutqini tinglang. Mavzu: “Yolg‘on hech qachon axloqan oqlanmaydi”. Notiq bu da’voga qarshi. Olti qadamni kuzating: da’vo, sabab, misol, raqibning eng kuchli e’tirozi, rad etish va qayta ta’kidlash. Mantiqiy bog‘lovchilarga ham quloq soling.
scenes.say: I oppose the motion. Honesty matters, but it is not the only value. Suppose a frightened friend hides in your house and a man with a knife asks where she is. The strongest case for the motion is that every lie erodes trust. I accept that. Yet it does not follow that we must sacrifice a life to preserve a principle. Given that our duties can conflict, a blanket ban on lying is not wisdom but rigidity.
scenes.say_uz: Men taklifga qarshiman. Halollik muhim, lekin u yagona qadriyat emas. Faraz qiling, qo‘rqib ketgan dugonangiz uyingizga yashirinadi va pichoq ko‘targan odam u qayerdaligini so‘raydi. Taklif foydasidagi eng kuchli dalil shuki, har bir yolg‘on ishonchni yemiradi. Buni tan olaman. Ammo bundan biz tamoyilni saqlash uchun hayotni qurbon qilishimiz kerak degan xulosa chiqmaydi. Burchlarimiz to‘qnashishi mumkinligini hisobga olsak, yolg‘onni mutlaq taqiqlash donolik emas, qotib qolganlikdir.

scenes.title: Fikriy tajriba nima
board: thought experiment (fikriy tajriba)
Suppose that... · Imagine a world in which...
Let us assume, for the sake of argument, that...
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi nuqta: thought experiments, ya’ni fikriy tajribalar. Bu laboratoriyasiz tajriba: xayoliy vaziyat qurib, axloqiy sezgimizni sinaymiz. Ular maxsus iboralar bilan boshlanadi: “Suppose that…”, “Imagine a world in which…”, “Let us assume, for the sake of argument, that…”, ya’ni “bahs uchun faraz qilaylik”.
scenes.say: A thought experiment is an imagined scenario designed to test our intuitions. It isolates one variable, much as a scientist would, and asks: what should we say about this case, and why?
scenes.say_uz: Fikriy tajriba sezgilarimizni sinash uchun o‘ylab topilgan xayoliy vaziyat. U olim kabi bitta o‘zgaruvchini ajratadi va so‘raydi: bu holat haqida nima deyishimiz kerak va nega?

scenes.title: Trolleybus muammosi
board: The trolley problem (Philippa Foot, 1967)
Pull the lever: one dies instead of five.
Footbridge version (J. J. Thomson): push a man?
scenes.say_native: Eng mashhur misol: trolley problem. Uni Filippa Fut 1967-yilda taklif qilgan, Judit Jarvis Tomson rivojlantirgan. Vagon besh kishiga qarab ketmoqda, richagni bossangiz, u bir kishini o‘ldiradi. Ko‘pchilik richagni bosadi. Ammo ko‘prikdan bir odamni itarib yuborish kerak bo‘lsa, ko‘pchilik qarshi. Raqamlar bir xil, sezgi esa turlicha.
scenes.say: In the trolley problem, diverting a runaway trolley kills one person instead of five. Most people would pull the lever, yet refuse to push a man off a footbridge to achieve the same result. Why should the numbers matter in one case but not the other?
scenes.say_uz: Trolleybus muammosida boshqaruvsiz vagonni burish besh kishi o‘rniga bir kishini o‘ldiradi. Ko‘pchilik richagni bosadi, ammo xuddi shu natija uchun ko‘prikdan odamni itarishni rad etadi. Nega raqamlar bir holatda muhim-u, boshqasida emas?

scenes.title: Faraz grammatikasi
board: If you pulled the lever, one person would die.
If you were to push him... (more tentative)
Were you to push him... (formal inversion)
Suppose you had known... what would you have done?
scenes.say_native: Fikriy tajriba grammatikasi. Xayoliy holat uchun ikkinchi shart: “If you pulled the lever, one person would die”. “Were to” yanada ehtiyotkor: “If you were to push him”. Rasmiy uslubda inversiya: “Were you to push him”. O‘tmishdagi xayoliy holat uchun uchinchi shart: “Had you known, what would you have done?”
scenes.say: Thought experiments live in hypothetical grammar. If you pulled the lever, one person would die. Were you to push him, five would live. And for the past: had you known, what would you have done?
scenes.say_uz: Fikriy tajribalar faraziy grammatikada yashaydi. Agar richagni bossangiz, bir kishi o‘ladi. Agar uni itarsangiz, besh kishi tirik qoladi. O‘tmish uchun: agar bilganingizda, nima qilgan bo‘lardingiz?

scenes.title: Tajriba mashinasi
board: The experience machine (Robert Nozick, 1974)
Would you plug in for life?
scenes.say_native: Endi ikkinchi mashhur fikriy tajribani tinglang. Uni amerikalik faylasuf Robert Nozik 1974-yilda taklif qilgan. Tinglayotganda o‘zingizdan so‘rang: siz bu mashinaga ulanardingizmi? Javobingiz baxt haqidagi qarashingiz haqida nima deydi? Faraz grammatikasiga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Imagine a machine that could give you any experience you desired. Neuroscientists would stimulate your brain so that you would think you were writing a great novel or falling in love, while in fact you were floating in a tank. Would you plug in for life? If not, it seems that we value something beyond pleasant experiences: perhaps actually doing things, or being in contact with reality.
scenes.say_uz: Sizga istagan har qanday tajribani bera oladigan mashinani tasavvur qiling. Neyrologlar miyangizni shunday qo‘zg‘atadiki, siz buyuk roman yozayotgan yoki sevib qolgan deb o‘ylaysiz, aslida esa idishda suzib yotgan bo‘lasiz. Butun umrga ulanardingizmi? Agar yo‘q bo‘lsa, demak biz yoqimli kechinmalardan boshqa narsani ham qadrlaymiz: ehtimol, haqiqatan ish qilishni yoki voqelik bilan aloqani.

scenes.title: Fikriy tajribaga javob berish
board: My intuition is that... · Intuitively, ...
What this case reveals is...
One could bite the bullet and say...
The analogy breaks down because...
scenes.say_native: Fikriy tajribaga qanday javob beramiz? Avval sezgingizni ayting: “My intuition is that I would not plug in”. Keyin tamoyil chiqaring: “What this case reveals is…”. Nazariyangiz noqulay xulosaga olib kelsa ham undan qaytmasangiz, bu “bite the bullet”. Tanqid uchun esa: “The analogy breaks down because…”
scenes.say: Respond in three moves: state your intuition, extract the principle it reveals, and test whether the case is a fair analogy. To bite the bullet is to accept an uncomfortable conclusion rather than abandon your theory.
scenes.say_uz: Uch qadamda javob bering: sezgingizni ayting, u ochib bergan tamoyilni chiqaring va holat adolatli o‘xshatish ekanini tekshiring. Bite the bullet nazariyadan voz kechish o‘rniga noqulay xulosani qabul qilishni bildiradi.

scenes.title: Shart gapdagi xatolar
board: ✗ If you would pull the lever, one would die.
✓ If you pulled the lever, one would die.
✗ Suppose you will see a drowning child.
✓ Suppose you saw a drowning child.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek o‘quvchilari shart gapda “would” ni ikkala qismga qo‘yadi: “If you would pull”. To‘g‘risi: “If you pulled”. “Suppose” dan keyin ham xayoliy holatda o‘tgan shakl: “Suppose you saw”. O‘zbekcha “-sa” qo‘shimchasi zamonni ko‘rsatmagani uchun bu xato tabiiy, lekin C2 darajasida sezilarli.
scenes.say: In a hypothetical, the if-clause takes a past form, not would: if you pulled, not if you would pull. Likewise, suppose you saw a drowning child, not suppose you will see.
scenes.say_uz: Faraziy gapda if qismi would emas, o‘tgan shakl oladi: if you pulled, if you would pull emas. Xuddi shunday, suppose you saw a drowning child deyiladi, suppose you will see emas.

scenes.title: Farazga aylantiring
board: 1 You push the man. Five people live. (2nd conditional)
2 Formal inversion of: If you were to lie, ...
3 You knew the truth. Did you act? (3rd conditional)
scenes.say_native: Uchta topshiriq. Birinchisini ikkinchi shartga aylantiring. Ikkinchisida “If you were to lie” ni rasmiy inversiya bilan boshlang va gapni tugating. Uchinchisida o‘tmishdagi xayoliy savol tuzing: agar haqiqatni bilganingizda, nima qilgan bo‘lardingiz? Javoblarni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: One: you push the man; five people live. Make it hypothetical. Two: rewrite if you were to lie with formal inversion. Three: you knew the truth; ask what you would have done.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: siz odamni itarasiz, besh kishi tirik qoladi. Farazga aylantiring. Ikki: if you were to lie ni rasmiy inversiya bilan qayta yozing. Uch: siz haqiqatni bilgansiz, nima qilgan bo‘lardingiz deb so‘rang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 If you pushed the man, five people would live.
2 Were you to lie, you would betray their trust.
3 Had you known the truth, what would you have done?
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “If you pushed the man, five people would live”, if qismida o‘tgan shakl, asosiy qismda would. Ikkinchi: “Were you to lie, you would betray their trust”, ya’ni “if” tushib qoladi va “were” oldinga chiqadi. Uchinchi: “Had you known the truth, what would you have done?”, bu ham inversiya, “If you had known” ning rasmiy shakli.
scenes.say: If you pushed the man, five people would live. Were you to lie, you would betray their trust. Had you known the truth, what would you have done?
scenes.say_uz: Agar odamni itarsangiz, besh kishi tirik qolardi. Agar yolg‘on gapirsangiz, ularning ishonchiga xiyonat qilgan bo‘lardingiz. Agar haqiqatni bilganingizda, nima qilgan bo‘lardingiz?

scenes.title: Yon berib, e’tiroz bildirish
board: I take your point, but...
That's a fair point; however, ...
I accept that X. What I'd dispute is Y.
There's something in that, although...
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi nuqta: hurmat bilan e’tiroz bildirish. Eng samarali usul: avval yon berish, keyin e’tiroz. “I take your point, but…”, “That’s a fair point; however…”. Aniqroq shakli: “I accept that lying erodes trust. What I’d dispute is that it’s always wrong”. Nimaga qo‘shilishingiz va nimaga qo‘shilmasligingiz aniq ajratilgan.
scenes.say: The most effective disagreement begins with concession. Separate precisely what you accept from what you dispute: I accept that lying erodes trust; what I'd dispute is the claim that it is always wrong.
scenes.say_uz: Eng samarali e’tiroz yon berishdan boshlanadi. Nimani qabul qilishingiz va nimaga e’tiroz bildirishingizni aniq ajrating: yolg‘on ishonchni yemirishini qabul qilaman, lekin u doim noto‘g‘ri degan da’voga qo‘shilmayman.

scenes.title: Yumshatish vositalari
board: I'm not entirely convinced that...
I'd question the assumption that...
I wonder whether that holds in every case.
With respect, I see it rather differently.
scenes.say_native: Akademik bahsda “No, you are wrong” juda qo‘pol eshitiladi. Yumshatilgan iboralar: “I’m not entirely convinced that…”, “I’d question the assumption that…”, “I wonder whether that holds in every case”. “With respect” ham muloyim ko‘rinadi, lekin Britaniyada ko‘pincha jiddiy e’tirozdan oldin keladi.
scenes.say: English debate relies heavily on understatement. I'm not entirely convinced often means I disagree completely. Note that with respect, in British usage, usually signals that a firm objection is coming.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz bahsi understatement ga, ya’ni yumshatib aytishga ko‘p tayanadi. I’m not entirely convinced ko‘pincha umuman qo‘shilmayman degani. Britaniya uslubida with respect odatda qat’iy e’tiroz kelayotganini bildiradi.

scenes.title: Aniqlashtirish va savol berish
board: What exactly do you mean by 'natural'?
Doesn't that presuppose that...?
Would you say the same about...?
Where would you draw the line?
scenes.say_native: Hurmatli bahsning yana bir quroli savol. Atamani aniqlashtiring: “What exactly do you mean by natural?” Yashirin asosni oching: “Doesn’t that presuppose that…?” Izchillikni sinang: “Would you say the same about…?” Chegarani so‘rang: “Where would you draw the line?” Savol hujum emas, taklif.
scenes.say: Questions are often more persuasive than assertions. Ask for definitions, expose hidden assumptions and test consistency: would you say the same about animals? Where exactly would you draw the line?
scenes.say_uz: Savollar ko‘pincha da’volardan ishonarliroq. Ta’rif so‘rang, yashirin taxminlarni oching va izchillikni sinang: hayvonlar haqida ham shunday derdingizmi? Chegarani aniq qayerdan o‘tkazardingiz?

scenes.title: Madaniy farq: to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘rilik
board: Uzbek: respect shown through form (siz, -lar)
English: respect shown through softening
Attack the idea, not the person
✗ You don't understand. ✓ Perhaps I haven't explained clearly.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida hurmat ko‘proq shakl orqali beriladi: “siz”, “-lar”, “aka”, “opa”. Ingliz tilida “you” hammaga bir xil, shuning uchun hurmat yumshatish orqali ifodalanadi. Shaxsga emas, fikrga qarshi chiqing. “You don’t understand” o‘rniga “Perhaps I haven’t explained this clearly” deng.
scenes.say: Since English has a single you, courtesy is carried by phrasing rather than grammar. Criticise positions, not people, and take responsibility for misunderstandings: perhaps I haven't put that clearly.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida yagona you bo‘lgani uchun xushmuomalalikni grammatika emas, ifoda tashiydi. Odamlarni emas, qarashlarni tanqid qiling va tushunmovchilik uchun mas’uliyatni oling: balki men buni aniq aytmagandirman.

scenes.title: E’tirozdagi xatolar
board: ✗ I am disagree with you.
✓ I disagree with you. / I don't agree.
✗ You are wrong. Your idea is stupid.
✓ I see it differently. I'm not sure that follows.
scenes.say_native: Ikki tipik xato. Birinchisi grammatik: “I am disagree”. “Disagree” fe’l, shuning uchun “am” kerak emas: “I disagree” yoki “I don’t agree”. Xuddi shunday “I am agree” ham xato. Ikkinchisi pragmatik: “You are wrong”, “Your idea is stupid” kabi to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri hujum. Grammatik to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa ham, akademik bahsda bu obro‘ingizni tushiradi.
scenes.say: Agree and disagree are verbs, so we say I disagree, never I am disagree. And blunt verdicts like you are wrong close a conversation, whereas I see it differently keeps it open.
scenes.say_uz: Agree va disagree fe’llar, shuning uchun I disagree deymiz, hech qachon I am disagree emas. You are wrong kabi keskin hukmlar suhbatni yopadi, I see it differently esa uni ochiq qoldiradi.

scenes.title: Yumshatib ayting
board: 1 You're wrong.
2 That's a stupid example.
3 I am disagree with your conclusion.
4 Your argument makes no sense.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta qo‘pol gapni muloyim, lekin aniq e’tirozga aylantiring. Bugun o‘rgangan iboralarni ishlating: yon berish, yumshatish yoki savol. Uchinchi gapda grammatik xatoni ham tuzating. Har biriga kamida bitta variant toping, pauza oling va baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Make these blunt statements respectful but clear. One: You're wrong. Two: That's a stupid example. Three: I am disagree with your conclusion. Four: Your argument makes no sense.
scenes.say_uz: Bu keskin gaplarni hurmatli, lekin aniq qiling. Bir: Siz noto‘g‘risiz. Ikki: Bu ahmoqona misol. Uch: Men xulosangizga qo‘shilmayman (xato shaklda). To‘rt: Dalilingiz ma’nosiz.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1 I'm not entirely convinced that's the case.
2 I wonder whether that example is representative.
3 I disagree with your conclusion.
4 I'm not sure I follow. Could you explain how X leads to Y?
scenes.say_native: Mumkin bo‘lgan javoblar. Birinchi: “I’m not entirely convinced that’s the case”. Ikkinchi: “I wonder whether that example is really representative”, ya’ni misolning umumiyligini shubha ostiga olamiz. Uchinchi: grammatikani tuzatamiz: “I disagree”. To‘rtinchi: aybni o‘zimizga olib, savol beramiz.
scenes.say: I'm not entirely convinced that's the case. I wonder whether that example is really representative. I disagree with your conclusion. And: I'm not sure I follow; could you explain how one point leads to the other?
scenes.say_uz: Bu shunday ekaniga to‘liq ishonmayman. Bu misol haqiqatan umumiy holatni aks ettiradimi, bilmadim. Xulosangizga qo‘shilmayman. Va: tushunmadim shekilli, bir fikr ikkinchisiga qanday olib kelishini tushuntira olasizmi?

scenes.title: Dialog: yolg‘on va burch
board: Leila · Tom
Is it ever right to lie to protect someone?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Ikki talaba, Leyla va Tom, yolg‘on haqida bahslashadi. Uch narsaga quloq soling: Tom qaysi yondashuvni himoya qiladi, Leyla qanday yon beradi va Tom qaysi savol bilan javob qaytaradi. Muloyim iboralarni eslab qoling, ular keyin kerak bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Tom: I'd hold that lying is wrong, full stop. If everyone lied when it suited them, trust would collapse. Leila: I take your point about trust, but surely saving a life outweighs a principle? Tom: Then where would you draw the line? A white lie to spare feelings? Leila: That's a fair question. I'd say only when serious harm is at stake.
scenes.say_uz: Tom: Menimcha, yolg‘on noto‘g‘ri, vassalom. Agar hamma o‘ziga qulay bo‘lganda yolg‘on gapirsa, ishonch qulaydi. Leyla: Ishonch haqidagi fikringizni tushunaman, lekin hayotni saqlab qolish tamoyildan ustun emasmi? Tom: Unda chegarani qayerdan o‘tkazasiz? Birovning ko‘nglini ayash uchun oq yolg‘onmi? Leyla: Bu o‘rinli savol. Menimcha, faqat jiddiy zarar xavfi bo‘lganda.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 Which approach does Tom defend?
2 How does Leila concede before disagreeing?
3 What question does Tom use to challenge her?
4 Where does Leila finally draw the line?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Birinchi: Tom qaysi axloqiy yondashuvni himoya qiladi? Ikkinchi: Leyla e’tirozdan oldin qaysi ibora bilan yon beradi? Uchinchi: Tom unga qaysi savol bilan qarshi chiqadi? To‘rtinchi: Leyla oxirida chegarani qayerdan o‘tkazadi? Inglizcha javob bering.
scenes.say: One: Which approach does Tom defend? Two: How does Leila concede before disagreeing? Three: What question does Tom use to challenge her? Four: Where does Leila finally draw the line?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Tom qaysi yondashuvni himoya qiladi? Ikki: Leyla e’tirozdan oldin qanday yon beradi? Uch: Tom unga qaysi savol bilan qarshi chiqadi? To‘rt: Leyla oxirida chegarani qayerdan o‘tkazadi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 a deontological view: lying is wrong in itself
2 I take your point about trust, but...
3 Where would you draw the line?
4 only when serious harm is at stake
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: Tom deontologik qarashni himoya qiladi, “full stop”, garchi ishonch haqidagi dalili natijaga tayansa ham. Ikkinchi: “I take your point about trust, but…”. Uchinchi: “Where would you draw the line?” To‘rtinchi: faqat jiddiy zarar xavfi bo‘lganda. “That’s a fair question” ham hurmat belgisi.
scenes.say: Tom takes a broadly deontological line, although his point about trust appeals to consequences. Leila concedes with I take your point about trust, Tom challenges her with where would you draw the line, and she limits lying to cases of serious harm.
scenes.say_uz: Tom umuman deontologik yo‘lni tutadi, garchi uning ishonch haqidagi fikri oqibatlarga murojaat qilsa ham. Leyla I take your point about trust bilan yon beradi, Tom where would you draw the line bilan qarshi chiqadi, Leyla esa yolg‘onni jiddiy zarar holatlari bilan cheklaydi.

scenes.title: Dialog: cho‘kayotgan bola
board: Chair · Dr Patel · Mr Hughes
Are the rich morally obliged to give to charity?
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog: radio munozarasi. Mavzu: boylar xayriya qilishga axloqan majburmi? Doktor Patel avstraliyalik faylasuf Piter Singerning 1972-yilgi mashhur fikriy tajribasiga tayanadi. Quloq soling: tajriba nimadan iborat, janob Hyuz qaysi joyda o‘xshatish buziladi deydi va Patel qanday javob beradi.
scenes.say: Dr Patel: Suppose you passed a shallow pond and saw a child drowning. You'd wade in, even if it ruined your expensive shoes. Distance, I'd argue, makes no moral difference. Mr Hughes: With respect, the analogy breaks down. I'm the only one at the pond, whereas millions could help a distant stranger. Dr Patel: But does the fact that others could help reduce my duty? I'm not convinced it does.
scenes.say_uz: Doktor Patel: Faraz qiling, sayoz hovuz yonidan o‘tib, cho‘kayotgan bolani ko‘rdingiz. Qimmat poyabzalingiz buzilsa ham suvga tushardingiz. Menimcha, masofa axloqan hech narsani o‘zgartirmaydi. Janob Hyuz: Uzr, lekin o‘xshatish buziladi. Hovuz yonida faqat men bor, uzoqdagi notanishga esa millionlab odam yordam bera oladi. Doktor Patel: Ammo boshqalar yordam bera olishi mening burchimni kamaytiradimi? Bunga ishonchim komil emas.

scenes.title: Munozara bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 What would you sacrifice to save the child?
2 What principle does Dr Patel draw from the case?
3 Why does Mr Hughes say the analogy breaks down?
4 How does Dr Patel respond?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Birinchi: bolani qutqarish uchun nima qurbon qilinadi? Ikkinchi: Patel bu holatdan qanday tamoyil chiqaradi? Uchinchi: Hyuz nega o‘xshatish buziladi deydi? To‘rtinchi: Patel qanday javob beradi va qaysi yumshatilgan ibora bilan? Javoblarni inglizcha ayting.
scenes.say: One: What would you sacrifice to save the child? Two: What principle does Dr Patel draw from the case? Three: Why does Mr Hughes say the analogy breaks down? Four: How does Dr Patel respond?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Bolani qutqarish uchun nima qurbon qilinadi? Ikki: Patel bu holatdan qanday tamoyil chiqaradi? Uch: Hyuz nega o‘xshatish buziladi deydi? To‘rt: Patel qanday javob beradi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 expensive shoes
2 Distance makes no moral difference.
3 At the pond only he can help; millions could help a stranger.
4 Does that reduce my duty? I'm not convinced it does.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: qimmat poyabzal. Ikkinchi: masofa axloqiy farq yaratmaydi. Uchinchi: hovuz yonida faqat bitta odam bor, uzoqdagi odamga esa millionlab kishi yordam bera oladi. To‘rtinchi: Patel savol bilan javob beradi va “I’m not convinced it does” deb yumshatadi. Hyuzning “With respect” iborasiga ham e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: The sacrifice is a pair of expensive shoes. Patel's principle is that distance makes no moral difference. Hughes objects that only he can help at the pond, and Patel replies with a question, softened by I'm not convinced it does.
scenes.say_uz: Qurbonlik qimmat poyabzal. Patelning tamoyili: masofa axloqiy farq yaratmaydi. Hyuz hovuz yonida faqat u yordam bera olishini aytib e’tiroz bildiradi, Patel esa savol bilan javob beradi va uni I’m not convinced it does bilan yumshatadi.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: ta’kid va ohang
board: Contrastive stress: I didn't say it was WRONG; I said it was UNWISE.
Weak 'that': I'd argue that /ðət/...
Fall-rise for partial agreement: In ˅principle...
scenes.say_native: Talaffuz. Bahsda ta’kidli urg‘u muhim: “I didn’t say it was WRONG; I said it was UNWISE”, qarama-qarshi so‘zlar kuchli urg‘u oladi. “I’d argue that” da “that” kuchsiz, “ðət” deb aytiladi. Qisman rozilikni tushib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang bildiradi: “In principle…” desangiz, tinglovchi “lekin” kelishini sezadi.
scenes.say: I didn't say it was wrong; I said it was unwise. I'd argue that distance is irrelevant. In principle, yes, but in practice, I'm not so sure.
scenes.say_uz: Men buni noto‘g‘ri demadim, oqilona emas dedim. Menimcha, masofa ahamiyatsiz. Nazariy jihatdan ha, lekin amalda unchalik ishonchim yo‘q.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: kirish nutqi
board: Motion: It is wrong to eat animals when alternatives exist.
60 seconds: claim · reason · thought experiment
steelman · rebuttal · restate
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy topshiriq. Mavzu: “Muqobil oziq-ovqat bo‘lsa, hayvonlarni yeyish noto‘g‘ri”. Tarafingizni tanlang va bir daqiqalik kirish nutqini ayting. Unda da’vo, sabab, bitta “Suppose…” bilan boshlanadigan fikriy tajriba, raqibning eng kuchli dalili, uni rad etish va qayta ta’kidlash bo‘lsin. Kamida bitta “it does not follow that” ishlating.
scenes.say: Final task. The motion: it is wrong to eat animals when alternatives exist. Choose a side and give a one-minute opening statement with a thought experiment, a steelman and a rebuttal.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy topshiriq. Taklif: muqobil bo‘lsa, hayvonlarni yeyish noto‘g‘ri. Tarafni tanlang va fikriy tajriba, steelman va rad etishdan iborat bir daqiqalik kirish nutqini ayting.

scenes.title: Namuna nutq
board: Claim → suffering matters
Thought experiment: a pleasure that requires pain
Steelman: tradition and culture → It does not follow...
scenes.say_native: Namunani tinglang va o‘zingiznikiga solishtiring. Notiq taklifni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi, “Suppose” bilan fikriy tajriba quradi, keyin raqibning eng kuchli dalilini, ya’ni an’ana va madaniyatni tan oladi va “it does not follow that” bilan rad etadi. Sizning nutqingizda boshqa taraf yoki boshqa misol bo‘lishi mumkin, muhimi olti qadam va hurmatli ohang.
scenes.say: I support the motion. Suppose a pleasure of yours required another creature to suffer, and an equally satisfying option did not. Would you still choose the first? The strongest objection is that food is bound up with culture and tradition. I accept that. But it does not follow that tradition justifies avoidable suffering.
scenes.say_uz: Men taklifni qo‘llab-quvvatlayman. Faraz qiling, sizning bir lazzatingiz boshqa jonzotning azoblanishini talab qiladi, xuddi shunday yoqimli boshqa variant esa talab qilmaydi. Baribir birinchisini tanlaysizmi? Eng kuchli e’tiroz shuki, taom madaniyat va an’ana bilan bog‘liq. Buni tan olaman. Lekin bundan an’ana oldini olish mumkin bo‘lgan azobni oqlaydi degan xulosa chiqmaydi.

scenes.title: Takrorlash
board: Vocabulary: autonomy, dignity, intrinsic value (no 'the' in general sense)
Logic: premises → conclusion · steelman · name the fallacy
Thought experiments: Suppose... / Were you to...
Disagree: concede → dispute · soften · question
scenes.say_native: Jamlaymiz. Birinchi: mavhum atamalarni aniq va umumiy ma’noda artiklsiz ishlating. Ikkinchi: dalil asoslardan xulosaga boradi, raqibning eng kuchli fikrini tan olib, keyin rad eting. Uchinchi: fikriy tajribalarni to‘g‘ri shart grammatikasi bilan bayon qiling. To‘rtinchi: avval yon bering, keyin yumshoq, ammo aniq e’tiroz bildiring.
scenes.say: To recap: use abstract terms precisely, build arguments from premises to conclusions, engage the strongest objection, frame thought experiments in hypothetical grammar and disagree by conceding first.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa: mavhum atamalarni aniq ishlating, dalilni asoslardan xulosaga quring, eng kuchli e’tiroz bilan ishlang, fikriy tajribalarni faraziy grammatikada bayon qiling va e’tirozni yon berishdan boshlang.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: debate an ethical dilemma for 3 minutes
Record yourself: both sides, 1 thought experiment
2 concessions · 3 connectors · 0 'I am disagree'
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: bitta axloqiy dilemmani tanlang va uch daqiqa bahs qiling, o‘zingizni yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: ikkala taraf dalili, bitta fikriy tajriba, kamida ikkita yon berish, uchta mantiqiy bog‘lovchi va birorta qo‘pol ibora yo‘q. Keyingi darsda siyosat va xalqaro munosabatlar lug‘atini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: For homework, debate an ethical dilemma for three minutes, presenting both sides, one thought experiment, two concessions and three logical connectors. Next time we explore the language of politics and international relations.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: axloqiy dilemmani uch daqiqa muhokama qiling, ikkala tarafni, bitta fikriy tajribani, ikkita yon berishni va uchta mantiqiy bog‘lovchini kiriting. Keyingi safar siyosat va xalqaro munosabatlar tilini o‘rganamiz.

homework_uz: Bitta axloqiy dilemmani (masalan, yolg‘on, hayvonlar yoki xayriya) tanlab, 3 daqiqa davomida inglizcha munozara qiling va o‘zingizni yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: ikkala tarafning dalili, bitta fikriy tajriba (Suppose... / Were you to...), kamida ikkita yon berish, uchta mantiqiy bog‘lovchi va birorta ham qo‘pol yoki “I am disagree” kabi xato ibora yo‘q.

quiz.q: Which view judges actions solely by their outcomes?

options: The freedom is essential in a democracy.
Freedom is essential in a democracy.
A freedom is essential in a democracy.
Freedoms is essential in a democracy.
quiz.why_uz: Umumiy ma’nodagi mavhum ot artiklsiz ishlatiladi.

quiz.q: 'He acted against his ___.' (his inner moral sense)
'If we legalise this, society will soon collapse.' Which fallacy is this?
quiz.why_uz: Bir qadamdan falokatgacha asossiz zanjir sirpanchiq yo‘l deyiladi.

quiz.q: 'You can't trust his view; he's rich.' This is...
quiz.why_uz: Fikr emas, shaxs tanqid qilinmoqda: ad hominem.

options: If you would push him, five would live.
If you push him, five would live.
If you pushed him, five would live.
If you will push him, five would live.
quiz.why_uz: Ikkinchi shartda if qismida o‘tgan shakl, asosiy qismda would.

quiz.q: Which is the correct formal inversion?
options: Were you to lie, you would lose their trust.
You were to lie, you would lose their trust.
Would you lie, you were to lose their trust.
Were you lie, you would lose their trust.
quiz.why_uz: Rasmiy inversiya: If you were to lie → Were you to lie.
Disagree fe’l, oldidan am kerak emas.

quiz.q: Which is the most respectful way to disagree?
options: I take your point, but I'd question the assumption that distance matters.
quiz.why_uz: Avval yon berish, keyin yumshatilgan e’tiroz hurmatli bahsning asosi.

quiz.q: Presenting your opponent's view in its strongest form is called...
quiz.why_uz: Steelman raqib fikrini eng kuchli shaklda bayon qilish, straw man ning aksi.
